hints: Focus on what cold, dilute versus hot, concentrated KMnO4 actually does to a C=C bond, gentle addition or full cleavage?
Notice retinol has several C=C bonds where each carbon is attached to either H or alkyl groups, so cleavage would first give aldehydes and ketones.
Remember what happens to an aldehyde under hot, concentrated oxidising conditions, and whether a ketone can be oxidised further.
walkthrough:
**Recall the two different KMnO4 conditions**

Cold, dilute acidified KMnO4 gives mild oxidation. Alkenes form diols, the C=C bond stays intact as C-C.

Hot, concentrated acidified KMnO4 gives vigorous oxidation. It breaks the C=C bond completely, this is oxidative cleavage.

**Choose the condition for breaking C=C**

The question says the C=C bonds are broken apart. That must be vigorous cleavage.

Condition needed:
$$\text{hot, concentrated KMnO}_4\text{(aq), H}^+$$

**Work out the first cleavage fragments from retinol**

Look at the chain in retinol. Each C=C is of the type $\text{RCH=CR}_2$ or similar.

General rule for cleavage:
$$\text{RCH=} \rightarrow \text{RCHO (an aldehyde)}$$
$$\text{R}_2\text{C=} \rightarrow \text{R}_2\text{C=O (a ketone)}$$

**Allow further oxidation under hot conditions**

Hot, concentrated KMnO4 is a very strong oxidiser, so aldehydes do not survive.

They are oxidised further:
$$\text{RCHO + [O]} \rightarrow \text{RCOOH (carboxylic acid)}$$ 
Ketones have no H on the carbonyl carbon, so they resist further oxidation and remain as ketones. The primary alcohol $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ in retinol is also oxidised fully to $-\text{COOH}$.

So the final mixture includes ketones and carboxylic acids, with no aldehydes left.

options.A: Incorrect. Cold, dilute KMnO4 gives diol formation, not C=C cleavage. Also aldehydes would not survive strong oxidation, they would become carboxylic acids.
options.B: Incorrect on conditions. Cold, dilute KMnO4 does not break C=C bonds. The product list of ketones and carboxylic acids is correct for vigorous oxidation, but the condition is wrong.
options.C: Incorrect on products. Hot, concentrated is correct for cleavage, but aldehydes cannot be final products here. Under these vigorous conditions any aldehyde formed is further oxidised to a carboxylic acid.
options.D: Correct. Hot, concentrated acidified KMnO4 cleaves all the C=C bonds in retinol. Initial aldehyde fragments are further oxidised to carboxylic acids, while ketone fragments remain, so final products include ketones and carboxylic acids.
